body.statement: For every \(W\in\mathcal R_q\), the algorithm \(\mathsf{Enum}(W)\) emits every member of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{stab}}(W)\) exactly once. If \(c=|C|\) and \(e_C\) is the number of admissibility edges in block \(C\), its local screening time is \(\sum_C O((c^{1/2}e_C+cN_{\mathrm{adm}}(W_C))\operatorname{poly}(c,L))\), after which Cartesian-product output has \(O(q)\) delay per stable assignment. The claim is output-sensitive in the enumerated local matching fibers and does not assert polynomial delay in \(N_{\mathrm{stab}}(W)\) alone.
body.justification: The bound makes the positive algorithmic content exact without hiding rejected local matchings behind a polynomial-delay claim.
body.gap: Uno enumerates unfiltered perfect matchings, while prior local causal discovery does not integrate normalized Schur screening or SCC products.
body.consumer: The procedure is an exact fallback for stable matching frequencies when the largest feedback SCC is small.
body.proof_tex:
Assume \(W\in\mathcal R_q\). Rational equality testing determines the support arrows exactly. Graph search from each vertex determines mutual reachability, and mutual reachability is an equivalence relation whose classes are exactly \(\operatorname{SCC}(B)\); hence the first step of \(\mathsf{Enum}\) computes the required partition exactly in polynomial time. Next note that every principal SCC block is itself a valid rational stable-reference input. Indeed, in a topological SCC order, \(W\) and \(B\) are block triangular. Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass:rational\mbox{-}input}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:unit\mbox{-}diagonal}\) pass to every \(W_C\). Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:invertible\mbox{-}equations}\) and block-triangular determinant factorization imply
\[
 0\neq\det(W)=\prod_C\det(W_C),
\]
so every \(W_C\) is invertible. Likewise assumption \(\mathrm{ass:stable\mbox{-}reference}\) and block-triangular spectral factorization give \(\rho(B[C,C])<1\). Hence \(W_C\in\mathcal R_{|C|}\).

Fix a component \(C\) of size \(c\). Form the bipartite graph \(H_C\) with a column copy and a row copy of \(C\), putting an edge \((i,r)\) exactly when \((W_C)_{ri}\neq0\). A perfect matching of \(H_C\) is precisely a bijection \(i\mapsto\pi_C(i)\) for which
\[
 (W_C)_{\pi_C(i),i}\neq0\qquad(i\in C),
\]
and hence, by \(\mathrm{def:admissible\mbox{-}orbit}\), is precisely a member of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{adm}}(W_C)\).

Here is a canonical implementation of the stated alternating recursion. Order the columns and, within each column, the incident rows. At a prefix assigning the first \(k\) columns injectively, test each available incident row and recurse exactly when the residual bipartite graph has a perfect matching. The feasibility test is exact: repeatedly augment a current matching along an alternating path. If no augmenting path exists before all residual columns are matched, let \(S\) be the residual columns reachable from an unmatched column by alternating paths. Every row neighboring \(S\) is matched back into \(S\), while \(S\) contains the initial unmatched column, so \(|N(S)|<|S|\); an injection matching all columns is then impossible. If an augmenting path exists, flipping its alternating edges increases the matching size by one. Thus at most \(c\) augmentations, each found by a graph search scanning \(O(e_C)\) edges, decide feasibility in \(O(ce_C)\) elementary operations. Moreover, two perfect extensions of the same prefix have symmetric difference equal to a disjoint union of even alternating cycles. The ordered prefix branch selects the first edge on which two such extensions differ, so this recursion is equivalently an exact-once alternating-cycle recursion.

Every perfect matching determines one and only one root-to-leaf sequence of prefix choices, so it is emitted exactly once. Conversely, a leaf is emitted only after every prefix, including the full assignment, passed the extension test, so every emitted leaf is a perfect matching. To bound the recursion tree, associate each feasible prefix with its lexicographically least perfect-matching extension. For a fixed perfect matching there is at most one associated prefix at each of the \(c+1\) depths. Hence there are at most \((c+1)N_{\mathrm{adm}}(W_C)\) feasible prefixes. At most \(c\) candidate children are tested at each such prefix. Using \(e_C\le c^2\), the initial feasibility test and all recursive work are therefore bounded by
\[
 O\!\left(
    \bigl(c^{1/2}e_C+cN_{\mathrm{adm}}(W_C)\bigr)
    \operatorname{poly}(c,L)
 \right).
\]
The displayed polynomial absorbs the factors from at most \(c\) child tests, at most \(c\) augmentations, and exact arithmetic; the initial \(O(ce_C)\) term has the required form because \(ce_C=(c^{1/2}e_C)c^{1/2}\).

For completeness, the stability screening invoked by \(\mathsf{Enum}\) is exact and has polynomial bit complexity. For a locally admissible matching let
\[
 A=I_c-
 \operatorname{diag}\!\left((W_C)_{\pi_C(i),i}^{-1}:i\in C\right)
 P_{\pi_C}W_C.
\]
Every divisor is nonzero by admissibility, so \(A\) is rational and its encoding length is polynomial in \(c\) and \(L\). Consider the rational linear system
\[
 P-A^{\mathsf T}PA=I_c.
\]
If \(\rho(A)<1\), the series
\[
 P=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}(A^k)^{\mathsf T}A^k
\]
converges, is positive definite, and solves the system. Its solution is unique: if \(H=A^{\mathsf T}HA\), then
\[
 H=(A^k)^{\mathsf T}HA^k\longrightarrow0,
\]
because \(\rho(A)<1\), whence \(H=0\). The unique solution is rational because it is the solution of a nonsingular rational linear system. Conversely, if a positive-definite \(P\) solves the equation and \(Av=\lambda v\) for a nonzero complex vector \(v\), then
\[
 (1-|\lambda|^2)v^*Pv
 =v^*(P-A^{\mathsf T}PA)v
 =v^*v>0.
\]
Since \(v^*Pv>0\), this forces \(|\lambda|<1\). Thus
\[
 \rho(A)<1
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \text{the Lyapunov system has a positive-definite solution}.
\]
This equivalence also excludes the boundary \(\rho(A)=1\). Fraction-free elimination solves the \(c^2\)-variable rational system. Exact symmetric elimination then writes a positive-definite candidate as \(P=LDL^{\mathsf T}\), where \(L\) is invertible lower triangular and \(D\) is diagonal; the identity \(x^{\mathsf T}Px=(L^{\mathsf T}x)^{\mathsf T}D(L^{\mathsf T}x)\) shows directly that \(P\) is positive definite exactly when every diagonal pivot in \(D\) is positive. A zero pivot causes rejection and cannot occur for a positive-definite matrix. Clearing denominators and applying the determinant expansion bounds all intermediate integer lengths by a polynomial in \(c\) and \(L\); hence the test takes \(\operatorname{poly}(c,L)\) bit operations. Normalization and screening of all local matchings therefore preserve the preceding output-sensitive bound. Summing it over the SCCs gives exactly the claimed local screening time.

The screening retains each stable local assignment once. By \(\mathrm{thm:scc\mbox{-}factorization}\), restriction and concatenation give a bijection between the Cartesian product of these retained lists and \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{stab}}(W)\). A lexicographic mixed-radix counter visits every tuple once; updating the counter takes at most the number of components, and writing the concatenated permutation takes \(q\) entries. Hence, after local screening, each stable assignment is emitted exactly once with \(O(q)\) delay. The screening bound depends on \(N_{\mathrm{adm}}(W_C)\), including rejected matchings, so it makes no polynomial-delay claim in \(N_{\mathrm{stab}}(W)\) alone.
